summary: S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology, holding attested posts in 1982 as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, S. K. Ramanatha Sastri studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. His career included serving as a Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938 and temporary staff at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indologist and historian who earned his BA and MA from the University of Madras. He lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929).

Indologist and philosopher S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943) studied at SPG College, Thanjavur, and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, Professor at Presidency College, and Honorary Professor at Annamalai University (~1935–1941).

S. M. Natesa Sastri (1859–1906) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras, later working as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1884–1888).

S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After studying at National College, Bangalore, he completed his doctorate under Etienne Vermeersch at Ghent University, where he later served as Director (~1991–2017).
S. N. Savadi was an Indology scholar who held attested posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 1953 and 1969.
Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar worked in Indology. He held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and in 1942 as Supervisor of Collations.

Working in Indology, history, and archaeology, S. Rajavelu served as Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and Professor of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri (1893–1942) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan (1926–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, history, and archaeology. He served as Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre until 1999, when he joined the Chinmaya International Foundation.

S. Sankararama Sastri worked in Indology. He held attested posts as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library in 1943 and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala in 1944.

S. Srikanta Sastri (1904–1974) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna (~1923–1928), and spent his academic career at the University of Mysore (~1928–1960).

S. Swaminathan, an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist, studied under J. Sundaram. He served as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India until his retirement in 2013.

Saba Mahmood (1961–2018) studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University (PhD). Working in religious studies and anthropology, she held posts at the University of Chicago (~1999–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (2004).

Sabine Löhr studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing her MA and doctoral work under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.

Saburō Hasegawa (1906–1957) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1953–1957) and held a post at the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).

Sadajiro Sugiura (1871–1947) studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (PhD), and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College (1903), and Rikkyo University, where he became an honorary professor (1931–1932).

Said Reza Huseini is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, King's College London (~2015–2016), and Leiden University (~2017–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi (1921–1994) studied at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University under Mohammad Habib. He headed history at the University of Jammu and Kashmir (~1963–1966) and served as Reader at the Australian National University (1967–1986).
